Where fs.protected_regular is off, `curl -o` then writes into that user's file, and they can replace its contents after `gpg --show-keys` passes and before `sudo gpg --dearmor` (line 52) reads it. A key that wasn't checked then becomes apt's root of trust. Where protected_regular is on, curl fails outright on the planted file. Either way, the step that decides trust shouldn't depend on a path someone else can guess. (Cyber reviewer (Opus 5.5))
   Suggested fix: Use a private temporary file: `key=$(mktemp)` and `curl -fsSL https://deepthinker2001.github.io/cosmic-ext-nightlight/key.gpg -o "$key"`, then `gpg --show-keys --with-fingerprint "$key"`, `sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/cosmic-ext-nightlight.gpg "$key"` and `rm "$key"` (also in the "if it differs" line). Or download into the user's home directory, e.g. `~/nightlight-key.gpg`.
